questions.question:
In a certain code language,

'heard their voice' is coded as 'nu ca es',

'their car was heard' is coded as 'hy ta es nu',

'voice was heard' is coded as 'es ta ca'.

(Note: All codes are two letter codes only)

What is the probable code for 'heard car' in the given code language?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef80c439f927363b3a830c735ed60e5cb58406f3d787e730c901bd2cff4f59f9.png] 

Thus code for** "heard"** is **"es".**

code for** "car"** is** "hy".**

∴ Here, **'heard car' is coded as 'es hy' or 'hy es'.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"hy es".**

questions.question:
Six students Prateek, Sameer, Kabir, Ziya, Joseph, Kiran are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Prateek is an immediate neighbour of both Sameer and Kabir. Ziya is sitting second to the right of Sameer. Kiran is sitting third to the left of Kabir. Joseph is an immediate neighbour of both Ziya and Kabir.

Who is sitting to the immediate left of Joseph?
questions.solution:
**Given: **Six students Prateek, Sameer, Kabir, Ziya, Joseph, Kiran are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (not necessarily in the same order).

Ziya is sitting second to the right of Sameer.

Prateek is an immediate neighbour of both Sameer and Kabir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b867ed85444b427469dd401e2fb3c10af9067adf32f5dc4e80b8a8e669c18918.png] 

Kiran is sitting third to the left of Kabir.

Joseph is an immediate neighbour of both Ziya and Kabir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b17e6d584adc7e05f1e02eefa193fd9deb10c0c601520490eeb647ac4c65f248.png] 

So, **Ziya **is sitting to the immediate left of **Joseph.**

Hence, the correct answer is ***'Option 2'.***

questions.question:
Select the numbers from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

4, 11, 30, 67, 128, ?

Given below are three statements followed by three conclusions I, II and III. Considering the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically follows from the statements.

**Statement:**

All apples are bananas.

All grapes are bananas.

All bananas are plums.

**Conclusion:**

I. All apples are plums.

II. All grapes are plums.

III. Some grapes are bananas.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17fcb4f1a1775974d7895642eb497d9cc78a48057a48f6068420bbc1c80bc362.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All apples are plums → Follow (As all apples are bananas and all bananas are plums. So, as whole apples comes in bananas which whole comes in plums therefore it is definitely true)

II. All grapes are plums → Follow (As all grapes are bananas and all bananas are plums. So, as whole grapes comes in bananas which whole comes in plums therefore it is definitely true)

III. Some grapes are bananas → Follow (As all grapes are bananas. So, as whole grapes comes in bananas therefore it is definitely true)

∴ Here, all conclusions follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "**All conclusions follow**".
